svg.title: The coefficient identity relating this insertion to the actual fine-lattice discrepancy is algebraic. For a finite census, the new coarse insertions multiply as Q i(1 + ziQi). Extracting a prescribed multi-index coefficient sums over the subset of slots taken from this product; every other slot is the coefficient transported from the negative fine observable. Coefficient extraction commutes with each finite RG push by linearity and integrability. The resulting subset sum is exactly the joint fine/coarse difference polynomial. Integrating the push does not change its integral, and restoring the fine/coarse coupling gives the positive Wilson partition function times the discrepancy moment. This is the identity used before taking the all-copy coefficient in (AP4). Thus the comparison bound, its normalization, and its locality all refer to the same transported difference.
